findings.title: updateMany with empty data is a no-op, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is never bumped
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma only fills in `@updatedAt` when there are other fields to write. With no write arguments the query engine skips the UPDATE, so `updatedAt` on SelectedCalendar is never refreshed. The stated purpose ("Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential") is not achieved. The call still adds a DB round-trip on every webhook-driven cache refresh. Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or remove the call; the PR notes already say the frontend doesn't use this field.

findings.title: Deleting the cache doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing stale cache status
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In contrast, `disconnectMutation` invalidates it in `onSettled`. On pages where `onChanged` isn't provided (e.g. /apps/installed/calendar), and because the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated …" and the "Delete cached data" action after a successful deletion. Users get no feedback that the cache is gone. Add an `onSettled` that invalidates `connectedCalendars`.

findings.title: Authorization failure thrown as plain Error, surfaces as 500
findings.body: When the credential doesn't belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps plain errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. A legitimate not-found/forbidden case is therefore reported and logged as a server crash, and the client can't tell the two apart. Throw a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN` instead.

findings.title: Backfilled updatedAt = migration time makes existing caches appear freshly updated
findings.body: `ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" ... DEFAULT NOW()` stamps every existing CalendarCache row with the migration timestamp. The new UI shows "Last updated: <timestamp>" from this column. Right after deploy, every user with an existing cache will see it as freshly updated, even if the data is up to a month old (CACHING_TIME). That is misleading in a feature meant to show cache freshness. A better backfill would be something like `expiresAt - interval '30 days'`.

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL
findings.body: The auto-generated header says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." The statement below does add `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is false and will confuse anyone auditing migrations. Remove or correct it.

findings.title: Cache status counts expired entries that are never served
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for the credential with no `expiresAt >= now` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only returns non-expired rows. A credential whose cache has fully expired, and is therefore never used, will still show a cache status and a "Last updated" timestamp in the UI. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so the status reflects cache that is actually in effect.

findings.title: Handler bypasses calendar-cache feature gating by instantiating the real repository directly
findings.body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init`, which selects `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is disabled. As a result, the mock's new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is never used. Users whose team has calendar-cache disabled, but who still have leftover rows, will see cache status and delete actions. The handler also adds an unconditional groupBy query to every connectedCalendars request.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields
findings.body: The `Pick` for `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Neither field is read anywhere in this module. The type is part of the public `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` export (legacy export for @calcom/platform-libraries), so every caller must now select these columns or fail type-checking. To satisfy it, `findUnlockedUserForSession` in user.ts now loads these columns for every session. Revert the type widening unless something actually consumes the fields.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale and time format preference (12h/24h). Non-US users see a US-style date like 7/15/25, 4:06 PM inside an otherwise translated string. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (i18n.language) or the app's existing date formatting helpers.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is macOS-only; script fails on Linux and exits 0 on errors
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed syntax. On GNU sed, `''` is parsed as the (empty) script and the substitution expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails on Linux. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's cwd rather than the script location. `cleanup` always does `exit 0`, so rate-limit and URL-extraction failures report success.

findings.title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx via npx
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx`, but `tsx` isn't a declared dependency while `ts-node` still is. npx will download an unpinned tsx at runtime, or fail offline. The change is also unrelated to this feature. Add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep ts-node.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache authorization or cache status query
findings.body: The PR adds a mutation that deletes data scoped by an ownership check, plus a new groupBy repository method. There are no unit or integration tests for either. Cases worth covering: deleting another user's credential cache must be rejected, and `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` must return the max `updatedAt` per credential. The PR description itself notes end-to-end testing was not possible.
